newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Keppel pre-tax at new high in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Keppel pre-tax at new high in 1996.

text.p: The chairman of Singapore conglomerate Keppel Corp said on Thursday profits and revenue had hit new highs in 1996 with property and banking growth more than compensating a bad year for its ship repair business.
"The group has reached new highs in both revenue and pre-tax profits for 1996," said Keppel group chairman Sim Kee Boon.
Sim said group assets had risen to almost S$19.0 billion at the end of 1996 from S$16.0 billion a year earlier.
"We are in a happy position today. The ship repair business has been bad. But this has been more than offset by the growth in our property and banking and financial services businesses."
As a result of diversification and the greater relative contribution to profits from non-shipping areas, Keppel should no longer be regarded as a pure marine stock.
Non-marine operations had lifted the group in 1996, he said.
Sim was speaking at Keppel's annual dinner ahead of full year results, expected to be announced in March.
The group reported a full year net profit of Singapore $214.09 million in 1995, up 1.3 percent from S$211.37 in 1994.
Strategically, Keppel was working on how to take advantage of Singapore's economic recovery and booms in other regional economies, Sim said.

This would be done by working on major infrastructure projects, moving into telecommunications -- Keppel is already a partner in Singapore's new Mobile One cellular network -- and bidding for new rail contracts in Singapore, he said.

Keppel would step up its investment programme in member states of the Association of Southeast Asean Nations (ASEAN) and rationalise its Philippines operations under the guise of the Keppel Philippines Group.
More streamlining would occur across the group to respond to the need for new corporate branding and repositioning which was also announced on Thursday, said Sim.
Details of streamlining were not disclosed.
